requirements.title: The lease record
requirements.rationale: Gateway, expiry and remote providers all build on one durable lease row whose shape is fixed at issue.

criteria.condition: af-hub starts, whether the sandbox feature is on or off
criteria.action: create the sandbox_leases table with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so that running the schema initialisation twice on the same database succeeds and leaves existing rows unchanged
criteria.contract: InitSchema(db) returns nil on a fresh database and again on a database that already holds the table and its rows

setup: a fresh in-memory SQLite database
check.pseudocode: assert InitSchema(db)==nil; insert(row); assert InitSchema(db)==nil; assert select(row.id)==row

criteria.action: constrain the state column with a CHECK that accepts exactly leased, active, destroyed, expired and failed, and declare the token hash column UNIQUE and nullable
criteria.contract: an INSERT with state 'active', 'expired' or 'failed' succeeds; an INSERT with state 'bogus' fails; two rows with NULL token hash coexist; two rows with the same non-NULL hash are refused

setup: an initialised sandbox_leases table
check.pseudocode: for s in states: assert insert(state=s).err==nil; assert insert(state='bogus').err!=nil; assert insert(hash=nil) && insert(hash=nil); insert(hash='h'); assert insert(hash='h').err!=nil

criteria.action: for any issued lease, assign an id made of sbx_ followed by the lowercase hex encoding of 16 bytes from crypto/rand
criteria.contract: every id matches ^sbx_[0-9a-f]{32}$ and no two issued leases share an id

setup: a lease service with a real in-memory database and capacity high enough
check.pseudocode: ids=[issue().id for _ in range(N)]; assert all(re.match('^sbx_[0-9a-f]{32}$',i)); assert len(set(ids))==N

criteria.condition: a lease is issued
criteria.action: store the workspace slug, profile name, purpose, state leased, the profile snapshot (image, network, cpus, memory_mb, pids, disk_mb, require_landlock, required and optional secret names, fixed environment), the caller's labels exactly as given, the TTL in seconds, expires_at, created_by, created_at and updated_at, with sandbox_id, error, ended_at and end_reason NULL
criteria.contract: the stored row holds these values; reading it back after the in-memory profile is changed still returns the values captured at issue

setup: a service whose profile 'tools' has image, network, cpus, memory, pids, disk, landlock, required and optional secrets and a fixed env
an active workspace with the required secrets present
check.pseudocode: l=issue(...); profile.Image='changed'; row=read(l.id); assert row.image=='orig' && row.env==origEnv && row.sandbox_id==nil

criteria.action: set created_by to "admin" when the credential type is admin_token and to the credential's UserID otherwise
criteria.contract: a lease issued with an admin token reads created_by "admin"; one issued with an API key for user u1 reads created_by "u1"

setup: a lease service and an active workspace
check.pseudocode: assert issue(auth{admin_token}).created_by=='admin'; assert issue(auth{api_key,u1}).created_by=='u1'

criteria.action: write every timestamp column with apikit.FormatUTC from the service's injected clock, and set expires_at to created_at plus the lease TTL
criteria.contract: created_at, updated_at, expires_at and ended_at parse as RFC 3339 UTC; expires_at minus created_at equals ttl_seconds

setup: a service with a fixed injected clock at 2030-01-02T03:04:05Z
check.pseudocode: l=issue(ttl='30m'); assert l.created_at==FormatUTC(clock()); assert parse(l.expires_at)-parse(l.created_at)==1800s

criteria.action: never store a secret value or a plaintext lease token in any column of sandbox_leases
criteria.contract: after a lease is issued for a workspace whose required secret has a planted value, neither that value nor the issued token appears as a substring of any column of the row

setup: a workspace secret with a planted value 'PLANTED-VALUE-123' that the profile requires
a planted secret value, captured logs, and a lease issued and then listed, fetched and deleted
check.pseudocode:
resp=post(); row=selectAll(id); for col in row: assert 'PLANTED-VALUE-123' not in str(col) and resp.token not in str(col)
bodies=[post,list,get,adminlist,delete,422case]; assert all(secret not in b); assert token in bodies[0] and all(token not in b for b in bodies[1:]) and token not in logs

requirements.title: Access rules for every lease route
requirements.rationale: The lease routes follow merge's ordering so a PAT's missing scope and a disabled feature are reported without revealing which workspaces exist.

criteria.condition: a request to any lease route (POST, GET list, GET one, DELETE, or GET /api/v1/sandboxes) carries no credential
criteria.action: reject the request before any other check
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 in apikit's error envelope; no lease row is created or changed

setup: the sandbox feature on and an existing lease
no credential on the requests
check.pseudocode: for route in routes: assert call(route, noauth).status==401; assert count==1 and state=='leased'

criteria.condition: the sandbox feature is off
criteria.action: answer every authenticated request to any lease route with error_type sandboxes_disabled, before checking scopes or the workspace
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type "sandboxes_disabled" via apikit.WriteAPIErrorWithType

setup: routes registered with a disabled (nil) service
a PAT with no scopes and a nonexistent workspace slug
check.pseudocode: for route in routes: r=call(route,pat_noscope); assert r.status==404 && r.error_type=='sandboxes_disabled'

criteria.condition: the caller is a PAT without sandboxes:write on POST or DELETE, or without either sandboxes:read or sandboxes:write on a per-workspace GET
criteria.action: reject the request before looking up the workspace, including when the workspace does not exist
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 via apikit.WriteAPIError; no lease row is created or changed

setup: a PAT with only sandboxes:read, a PAT with no sandbox scope and a PAT with only sandboxes:write
a nonexistent workspace slug and an existing one
check.pseudocode: assert post(pat_read,'nosuch').status==403; assert get(pat_none,ws).status==403; assert get(pat_write,ws).status==200

criteria.condition: wsaccess.AuthorizeWorkspace refuses the slug because the workspace does not exist or the caller does not own it
criteria.action: reject the request without revealing whether the workspace exists, while admin tokens pass for any existing workspace
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 for a missing or unowned workspace; no lease row is created or changed

setup: workspace 'widgets' owned by user u1
an API key for user u2 and an admin token
check.pseudocode: assert post(u2,'widgets').status==404; assert post(u2,'nosuch').status==404; assert post(admin,'widgets').status==201; assert count==1

criteria.condition: POST targets a workspace whose status is not active
criteria.action: refuse to issue a lease
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with message "workspace is not active"; the sandbox_leases row count is unchanged

setup: a workspace with status 'archived' owned by the caller
check.pseudocode: r=post(); assert r.status==400 && r.msg=='workspace is not active'; assert count==before

criteria.condition: the workspace is archived
criteria.action: serve GET list, GET one and DELETE for its leases with the same results as for an active workspace
criteria.contract: GET answers 200 and DELETE answers 204 for an archived workspace's lease

setup: a lease issued while the workspace was active, then the workspace set to archived
check.pseudocode: archive(ws); assert get_list().status==200; assert get_one(id).status==200; assert delete(id).status==204

criteria.condition: a credential other than admin_token, including an API key or a PAT holding both sandbox scopes, calls GET /api/v1/sandboxes
criteria.action: refuse the admin list
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 via apikit.WriteAPIError

setup: an API key and a PAT holding both sandboxes:read and sandboxes:write
check.pseudocode: assert get('/api/v1/sandboxes',apikey).status==403; assert get(..., pat_both).status==403

requirements.title: Issuing a lease and validating the request body
requirements.rationale: A caller says which profile; hub says what is in it, so every field outside the four allowed ones is refused rather than silently ignored.

criteria.condition: an authorised caller sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes with {"profile":"tools"} for an active workspace whose required secrets exist, below capacity
criteria.action: store a lease in state leased and return the lease representation of 26-REQ-7.6 plus the token
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with body containing state "leased", profile "tools", the profile's image, network, resources and secret names, expires_at equal to created_at plus the profile TTL, and token

setup: an active workspace 'widgets' with the required secrets present, below capacity
profile 'tools' with a TTL of 1h
a recording audit emitter, a planted secret value, an active workspace
captured slog output
a fake hub HTTP server returning a 201 lease with a token
a path in a temp directory
check.pseudocode:
r=post({'profile':'tools'}); assert r.status==201 && r.json.state=='leased' && r.json.token!=''; assert parse(expires_at)-parse(created_at)==1h
post(); assert len(rec.events)==1 and e.Workspace==slug and e.Action=='lease'; assert token not in json(e) and token not in logs; svc.emitter=nil; assert post().status==201
out,err,_=run('sandbox','create','widgets','--token-file',p); assert stat(p).perm==0o600 and read(p)==tok; assert 'token' not in json(out)

criteria.condition: the POST body is empty, or is a JSON object without profile, ttl or purpose
criteria.action: treat an empty body as {}, use the profile spec 25 marks as default, the profile's TTL and an empty purpose
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with profile equal to the default profile's name, purpose "" and expires_at minus created_at equal to the profile TTL

setup: a configuration whose default profile is 'tools' with TTL 1h
check.pseudocode: for body in ['', '{}']: r=post(body); assert r.status==201 && r.profile=='tools' && r.purpose==''

criteria.condition: the POST body is not a JSON object, or contains a field other than profile, purpose, ttl and labels (for example image or env)
criteria.action: refuse the request, naming the unknown field when there is one
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 whose message contains the unknown field name; no lease row is stored

setup: an active workspace and a lease table that is empty
check.pseudocode: r=post({'image':'evil'}); assert r.status==400 && 'image' in r.msg; assert post('[1]').status==400; assert count==0

criteria.condition: profile names no configured profile under exact, case-sensitive comparison, or profile is absent and no profile is marked default
criteria.action: refuse the request and list the known profile names in configuration order
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 whose message contains every configured profile name in configuration order; no lease row is stored

setup: profiles configured in order 'tools','data' with no default marked for the second scenario
an active workspace
check.pseudocode: r=post({'profile':'Tools'}); assert r.status==400; assert idx(r.msg,'tools')<idx(r.msg,'data'); assert count==0

criteria.condition: ttl is a Go duration string and its value is at least 1 minute and at most the chosen profile's TTL
criteria.action: issue the lease with that TTL
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with expires_at equal to created_at plus ttl; ttl "1m" and ttl equal to the profile TTL are both accepted

setup: profile 'tools' with a TTL of 1h
check.pseudocode: for t in ['1m','15m','1h']: r=post({'ttl':t}); assert r.status==201 && parse(r.expires_at)-parse(r.created_at)==dur(t)

criteria.condition: ttl does not parse with time.ParseDuration, is shorter than 1 minute (including zero and negative values), or is longer than the chosen profile's TTL
criteria.action: refuse the request, and when the value is too long name the profile's TTL in the message
criteria.contract: HTTP 400; for a too-long ttl the message contains the profile TTL; no lease row is stored

setup: profile 'tools' with a TTL of 1h
check.pseudocode: for t in bad: assert post({'ttl':t}).status==400; assert '1h' in post({'ttl':'2h'}).msg; assert count==0

criteria.condition: purpose is longer than 64 runes or contains a control character
criteria.action: refuse the request, while accepting a purpose of exactly 64 runes
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for 65 runes or a control character; HTTP 201 for 64 runes; no lease row is stored on refusal

setup: an active workspace
check.pseudocode: assert post({'purpose':'é'*64}).status==201; assert post({'purpose':'a'*65}).status==400; assert post({'purpose':'a\nb'}).status==400

criteria.condition: labels has more than 16 pairs, a non-string value, a key that is not 1–63 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._-] starting and ending with a letter or digit, a key equal to lease or workspace in any case, or a value longer than 256 bytes or containing a control character
criteria.action: refuse the request, naming the offending label key
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 whose message contains the label key; 16 pairs, a 63-character key and a 256-byte value are accepted; no lease row is stored on refusal

setup: an active workspace and an empty lease table
an active workspace
check.pseudocode:
for labels in bad_cases: r=post({'labels':labels}); assert r.status==400 && badkey in r.msg; assert count==0
r=post({'labels':L}); assert r.status==201 && r.json.labels==L

requirements.title: Required-secret presence check
requirements.rationale: A lease whose box could never start for want of a secret should fail at POST, and the check must not be able to leak what it never reads.

criteria.condition: a POST passes request validation
criteria.action: before storing the lease, confirm that every name in the profile's required secrets exists in at least one scope of the workspace's resolution chain, reading key names only through secrets.Store.ListSecrets and never calling GetSecretValue
criteria.contract: the lease is stored only when every required name is found; the check performs zero GetSecretValue calls

setup: a secrets lister test double that records calls and exposes only ListSecrets
a profile with required secret GIT_PAT and optional secret EXTRA that exists nowhere
check.pseudocode: fake.add('workspace',slug,'GIT_PAT'); r=post(); assert r.status==201; assert fake.getValueCalls==0

criteria.action: match required secret names against stored key names case-insensitively, as GetSecretValue's UPPER(key) comparison does
criteria.contract: a profile requiring GIT_PAT is satisfied by a workspace secret stored as git_pat

setup: a profile requiring GIT_PAT
a workspace secret stored as git_pat
check.pseudocode: store('workspace',slug,'git_pat','v'); assert issue().err==nil

criteria.action: compute the resolution chain in one exported helper that returns, in order, the workspace scope (owner ID = slug), the org scope (owner ID = the workspace's org_id) only when org_id is set and the workspace owner has a row in org_members for that org, and the user scope of the workspace owner, never of the caller
criteria.contract: the helper returns [workspace, org, user] for an owner who is an org member, [workspace, user] when org_id is NULL or the owner is not a member, and the user entry always carries workspaces.owner_id even when an admin token calls

setup: workspace A with org_id O whose owner u1 is in org_members
workspace B with org_id O whose owner is not a member
workspace C with NULL org_id
check.pseudocode: assert chain(A)==[('workspace',A),('org','O'),('user','u1')]; assert chain(B)==[('workspace',B),('user',ownerB)]

criteria.condition: one or more required secret names exist in no scope of the resolution chain
criteria.action: refuse the lease, naming every missing key in profile order and the scope types searched, without naming the owner's user ID or the org ID
criteria.contract: HTTP 422 with error_type "secret_missing"; the message contains each missing key in profile order and the searched scope types (for example "workspace, user"); the sandbox_leases row count is unchanged

setup: a profile requiring A_KEY, B_KEY, C_KEY where only B_KEY exists in the owner's user scope
a workspace owner u1 with no org
check.pseudocode: r=post(); assert r.status==422 && r.error_type=='secret_missing'; assert idx(A_KEY)<idx(C_KEY); assert 'u1' not in r.msg; assert count==0

criteria.action: issue the lease without checking the presence of names listed only in the profile's optional_secrets
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 when every optional secret is absent and every required secret is present

criteria.condition: the secrets store or the workspace/org_members lookup returns an error during the check
criteria.action: refuse the lease
criteria.contract: HTTP 500; the sandbox_leases row count is unchanged

setup: a secrets lister that returns an error, and separately a database whose org_members table is missing
check.pseudocode: fake.err=errors.New('boom'); assert post().status==500; assert count==0; drop(org_members); assert post().status==500

requirements.title: Capacity limit max_sandboxes
requirements.rationale: A deployment must be able to bound how many sandboxes can be live at once, and concurrent issuance must not overshoot it.

criteria.condition: the [sandbox] section is present and has no max_sandboxes key
criteria.action: use 16 as max_sandboxes and accept the key without an unknown-key failure when it is present
criteria.contract: the effective limit is 16 when absent; a section with max_sandboxes = 3 loads with limit 3 and no unknown-key error

setup: a TOML [sandbox] section with profiles and no max_sandboxes
a TOML [sandbox] section with max_sandboxes = 3
check.pseudocode: assert load(noKey).MaxSandboxes==16; c,err=load('max_sandboxes=3'); assert err==nil && c.MaxSandboxes==3

criteria.condition: [sandbox].max_sandboxes is present and is not an integer of at least 1
criteria.action: refuse start with a failure naming [sandbox].max_sandboxes
criteria.contract: non-nil validation error containing "max_sandboxes" for 0, -1 or a non-integer; af-hub exits non-zero

setup: TOML sections with max_sandboxes = 0, -1 and 2.5
check.pseudocode: for v in [0,-1,2.5]: err=load(v); assert err!=nil && 'max_sandboxes' in err.Error()

criteria.action: count against capacity only leases in state leased or active whose expires_at is later than the injected clock's now, across all workspaces
criteria.contract: destroyed leases and leased rows whose expires_at is at or before now are excluded from the capacity count

setup: rows: leased future, active future, destroyed future, leased with expires_at equal to now, leased past, across two workspaces
a controllable clock
check.pseudocode: seed(rows); assert svc.countLive(now)==2

criteria.condition: the capacity count has reached max_sandboxes when a POST would store a lease
criteria.action: refuse the lease, naming the limit
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type "sandbox_capacity" and a message containing the max_sandboxes value; the sandbox_leases row count is unchanged

setup: max_sandboxes = 2 and two live leases (in any workspaces)
check.pseudocode: r=post(); assert r.status==409 && r.error_type=='sandbox_capacity' && '2' in r.msg; delete(first); assert post().status==201

criteria.action: for any number of concurrent POSTs against a limit M with K live leases, perform the capacity count and the insert under one in-process mutex and inside one database transaction, so that at most M minus K of them succeed
criteria.contract: after N concurrent POSTs the capacity count never exceeds M; each refused POST answers 409 sandbox_capacity

setup: a file-backed or shared SQLite database and a service with limit M and K existing live leases
check.pseudocode: results=parallel(N, post); assert count(201)==min(N,M-K); assert all(r.status in (201,409)); assert countLive()<=M

criteria.condition: the database returns an error while counting or inserting
criteria.action: roll back the transaction, release the mutex and refuse the lease
criteria.contract: HTTP 500; no partial lease row remains; a following POST is not blocked

setup: a database where the insert fails once (for example a trigger or closed-then-reopened handle)
check.pseudocode: inject_fault(); assert post().status==500; assert count==0; clear_fault(); assert post(timeout=2s).status==201

requirements.title: Lease token, lookup and revocation
requirements.rationale: The token is the credential sandbox_gateway authenticates; it must be unguessable, unrecoverable from storage and dead after revocation.

criteria.action: for any issued lease, generate the token as sbl_ followed by base64.RawURLEncoding of 33 bytes from crypto/rand
criteria.contract: every token is 48 characters and matches ^sbl_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{44}$

setup: a lease service with a real database
check.pseudocode: for t in tokens: assert len(t)==48 and re.match('^sbl_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{44}$',t); assert len(b64.decode(t[4:]))==33

criteria.action: store only the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the token
criteria.contract: the stored hash equals hex.EncodeToString(sha256.Sum256(token)) and matches ^[0-9a-f]{64}$

setup: an issued lease and its plaintext token
check.pseudocode: assert row.token_hash==hex(sha256(token)) and re.match('^[0-9a-f]{64}$',row.token_hash)

criteria.condition: reading random bytes for the lease id or the token fails
criteria.action: refuse the lease and store nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 500; the sandbox_leases row count is unchanged

setup: a service whose random reader returns an error
check.pseudocode: svc.rand=failingReader; assert post().status==500; assert count==0

criteria.condition: the lease store's token lookup is given a well-formed token whose hash matches a lease in state leased or active
criteria.action: return that lease
criteria.contract: the lookup returns the lease with the matching id and a nil error

setup: one lease in state leased and another in state active with known tokens
check.pseudocode: l,err=store.LookupByToken(tok); assert err==nil && l.ID==id

criteria.condition: the token given to the lookup is empty, lacks the sbl_ prefix, has the wrong length or alphabet, matches no stored hash, or belongs to a lease in a terminal state
criteria.action: report not found without distinguishing the cases
criteria.contract: the lookup returns a nil lease and the same not-found sentinel error in every case

setup: a live lease, a destroyed lease whose hash was retained by direct SQL, and an expired/failed lease
check.pseudocode: for t in cases: l,err=lookup(t); assert l==nil && err==ErrNotFound

criteria.condition: a lease's token is revoked
criteria.action: move the lease to a terminal state and set its token hash to NULL in the same UPDATE statement
criteria.contract: after revocation the row's token hash is NULL and every later lookup of that token returns not found

setup: a live lease with a known token
check.pseudocode: revoke(id); assert row.token_hash is NULL and row.state in terminal; assert lookup(tok).err==ErrNotFound

requirements.title: Reading leases
requirements.rationale: Callers and admins must be able to see what leases exist without ever seeing a token or an environment value.

criteria.condition: an authorised caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes
criteria.action: return the workspace's leases in state leased or active, newest created_at first, at most 200
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with a bare JSON array, [] (never null) when there are none, holding no lease of another workspace

setup: workspace 'widgets' with three live leases at different created_at, one destroyed lease, and a lease in another workspace
205 live leases in one workspace inserted directly
check.pseudocode:
r=get(list); assert ids(r)==[newest..oldest]; assert get(empty).body=='[]'
seed(205); assert len(get(list).json)==200

criteria.condition: the list request carries an all query parameter that strconv.ParseBool reads as true
criteria.action: include leases in terminal states in the list
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; a destroyed lease appears with ?all=true and not without it

setup: a live lease and a destroyed lease in the workspace
check.pseudocode: assert len(get(list).json)==1; assert len(get(list+'?all=true').json)==2

criteria.condition: the all query parameter is present and strconv.ParseBool cannot parse it
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for ?all=maybe on the workspace list and on GET /api/v1/sandboxes

setup: an owner credential and an admin token
check.pseudocode: assert get(list+'?all=maybe').status==400; assert get_admin('/api/v1/sandboxes?all=maybe').status==400

criteria.condition: an authorised caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id for a lease of that workspace
criteria.action: return that lease in any state
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the lease representation

setup: a leased lease and a destroyed lease in the workspace
check.pseudocode: assert get(id1).json.state=='leased'; assert get(id2).json.state=='destroyed'

criteria.condition: the lease id in GET one is malformed, unknown, or belongs to another workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request without distinguishing the cases
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with message "sandbox lease not found"

setup: a lease in workspace 'other' and the caller owning 'widgets'
check.pseudocode: for id in [bad, unknown, foreign]: r=get(id); assert r.status==404 && r.msg=='sandbox lease not found'

criteria.action: render every lease with exactly the fields id, workspace, profile, purpose, state, expires_at, image, network, resources {cpus, memory_mb, pids, disk_mb}, require_landlock, secrets, optional_secrets, labels, created_by, created_at, updated_at, sandbox_id, error, ended_at and end_reason, where secrets and optional_secrets are always arrays, labels is always an object and the last four are null until set
criteria.contract: no rendered lease from any GET contains token, the token hash or an environment value; secrets and optional_secrets render as [] when empty and labels as {}

setup: a lease from a profile with a fixed env {SECRET_ENV:'envval'}, no optional secrets and no labels
its token and token hash
check.pseudocode: j=get(id).json; assert set(j.keys())==EXPECTED; assert j.optional_secrets==[] and j.labels=={}; assert token not in raw and hash not in raw and 'envval' not in raw

criteria.condition: an admin token sends GET /api/v1/sandboxes while the feature is on
criteria.action: return every workspace's leases in the representation of 26-REQ-7.6, newest first, at most 200, live leases only unless ?all=true
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with a bare JSON array that includes leases of more than one workspace

setup: live leases in two workspaces and a destroyed lease
check.pseudocode: r=admin_get('/api/v1/sandboxes'); assert {l.workspace for l in r}=={'a','b'}; assert len(admin_get(...'?all=true'))==len(r)+1

requirements.title: Ending a lease
requirements.rationale: A caller must be able to give back a lease and revoke its token, and retries must be harmless.

criteria.condition: an authorised caller sends DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id for a lease of that workspace in state leased or active
criteria.action: set state to destroyed, ended_at and updated_at to now, end_reason to api, and token hash to NULL in one UPDATE conditioned on the state being leased or active
criteria.contract: HTTP 204 with empty body; GET one then reads state "destroyed" and end_reason "api"; token lookup returns not found

setup: a live lease whose token is known
a fake hub HTTP server answering 204 to DELETE
check.pseudocode:
assert delete(id).status==204 && body==''; j=get(id).json; assert j.state=='destroyed' && j.end_reason=='api'; assert lookup(tok).err==ErrNotFound
out,errOut,err=run('sandbox','destroy','widgets','sbx_x'); assert out_json=={'status':'destroyed','id':'sbx_x'}

criteria.condition: DELETE targets a lease of that workspace already in a terminal state
criteria.action: change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 204; ended_at, end_reason and updated_at keep their earlier values

setup: a lease already destroyed at an earlier time with end_reason 'api'
check.pseudocode: before=row(id); advance(clock); assert delete(id).status==204; assert row(id)==before

criteria.condition: the DELETE lease id is malformed, unknown, or belongs to another workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request and change no lease
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with message "sandbox lease not found"; the other workspace's lease is unchanged

setup: a live lease in another workspace owned by the same user
check.pseudocode: for id in cases: r=delete(id); assert r.status==404; assert row(foreign).state=='leased' and lookup(tok).err==nil

criteria.action: route every lease ending through one end-lease function that takes the lease, the target terminal state and the end reason, which the DELETE handler calls
criteria.contract: the live lease becomes destroyed with reason and cleared hash; the already-ended lease is untouched (conditional update affects zero rows); the DELETE handler's effect is identical to calling EndLease directly (the handler is a thin wrapper)

setup: a live lease and a destroyed lease
check.pseudocode: assert EndLease(live,'destroyed','api').changed==true; assert EndLease(done,'destroyed','api').changed==false

real_components: SQLite database (sandbox_leases, workspaces, org_members, secrets tables)
setup: the full route set registered on an echo group with real handlers, lease service, SQLite database, secrets store, workspace tables and audit emitter
